problem.heading.text: You have the document. Nobody can find it when it matters.

problem.lede.text: Four patterns repeat across regulated operations: the audit pull that takes days, the version that depends on where you look, the change the floor never hears about, and the retraining that arrives weeks late.

hero.sub.text: Document Control, Change Control, and Training on one governed record, from draft to obsolete.

ctax.heading.text: The work is rarely the bottleneck. The coordination is.

ctax.lede.text: In a regulated operation, a task seldom stalls because it is hard. It stalls in the gaps between people, documents, and systems: an approval waiting in an inbox, a version no one can vouch for, the same fact keyed into three tools that now disagree. Every gap is a tax, paid in time and in the ability to prove the work was done right.

problem.card1.title.text: Days to assemble one audit record

problem.card1.quote.text: When auditors ask for the full record we spend days pulling it together.

problem.card1.detail.text: Evidence is stitched from exports, screenshots, and email forwards. The audit passes; passing costs days of senior time each cycle.

problem.card2.quote.text: SOPs are written once and never updated even when the process changes.

problem.card2.detail.text: The controlled system says v3.2, a file share holds a local v3.1, and the workstation runs a laminated v2.8. The current version is a function of where you look.

problem.card3.title.text: The floor hears about the change last

problem.card3.quote.text: A change was approved months ago but has not been fully implemented anywhere.

problem.card3.detail.text: The line builds to the old version because the notification, the training, or the parts on hand lag the effective date. The first sign is a rejected part.

problem.card4.title.text: Retraining lands weeks after the change

problem.card4.quote.text: Retraining after a change is always late because nobody tracks who needs it.

problem.card4.detail.text: People work to the new version without verified training, and the trace between the change and the training is partial when the auditor asks.

modules.card1.blurb.text: Author, review, approve, distribute, and periodically review controlled documents with full version history.

modules.card2.blurb.text: Change orders and revisions routed through configurable approvals, with impact assessment on the record.

modules.card3.blurb.text: A revision cascades into the training obligation, so people are always current on the version they use.

capabilities.card1.body.text: Every revision retained under the edition it shipped.

capabilities.card2.body.text: Review dates that route to an owner and expect an attestation.

capabilities.card3.body.text: DRAFT, EFFECTIVE, OBSOLETE stamped on the render.

capabilities.card4.body.text: Signer, meaning, and timestamp where the record requires it.

capabilities.card5.body.text: Reverse-trace a document to everything that references it.

capabilities.card6.body.text: Read-only, watermarked, without handing over the library.

lifecycle.state1.detail.text: Authored from a controlled template with automatic numbering. Nothing reaches the floor from here: the render is watermarked DRAFT and cannot be distributed.

lifecycle.state2.detail.text: Routed to reviewers for technical accuracy. Comments and redlines stay on the record, so the review is part of the document's history, not an email thread.

lifecycle.state3.detail.text: QA signs with 21 CFR Part 11 meaning where the record requires it: signer, meaning of signature, and timestamp, permanently attached to the revision.

lifecycle.state4.detail.text: Watermarked EFFECTIVE and distributed. Training assignments open the moment it goes live, so people are current on the version they actually use.

lifecycle.state5.detail.text: The prior revision is retained read-only under the edition it shipped. Every historical version stays retrievable for the auditor who asks.

lifecycle.state6.detail.text: Distributed copies are retrieved and the record is archived per your retention policy. The watermark flips to OBSOLETE on every render.

flows.heading.text: Follow the work through the lifecycle.

flows.lede.text: See each role’s path from first action to final handoff.

integrations.diagram.heading.text: A controlled document is filed against the record it governs.

integrations.diagram.lede.text: A document never lives alone. Unifize sits over the ERP, PLM, and identity systems you already run, so a controlled document is filed against the real part, distributed to the real people, and never becomes a fourth copy.

faq.q1.question.text: What exactly is bundled in DMS?

faq.q1.answer.text: Three modules on one record: Document Control, Change Control, and Training Management. A change order drives the revision, and the revision drives the training assignment, without re-entry between tools.

faq.q2.question.text: Does it support 21 CFR Part 11 electronic signatures?

faq.q2.answer.text: Yes, where the record requires it. Approvals capture the signer, the meaning of the signature, and a timestamp, and the signature travels with the revision it approved.

faq.q3.question.text: What happens to superseded and obsolete revisions?

faq.q3.answer.text: Superseded revisions are retained read-only under the edition they shipped. When a document goes obsolete, distributed copies are retrieved and the record is archived per your retention policy.

faq.q4.question.text: How do auditors access the library?

faq.q4.answer.text: Through scoped, read-only, watermarked access. You share the document trees the audit needs without handing over the whole library.

faq.q5.question.text: How does training stay current with revisions?

faq.q5.answer.text: A new effective revision cascades into a training obligation for every role mapped to the document, so people are always trained on the version they actually use.

faq.q6.question.text: Which standards does the lifecycle map to?

faq.q6.answer.text: ISO 9001, ISO 13485, 21 CFR Part 11, 21 CFR Part 820, EU GMP, and WHO GMP. One controlled lifecycle, whatever you are audited against.
